learningObjective: Reason about the relative energy costs of on-chip compute vs off-chip memory access and their implications for DNN accelerator design.

canonicalClaims.claim: DRAM access energy is 2–3 orders of magnitude larger than an on-chip MAC in modern accelerators, so reducing off-chip data movement is the primary lever for energy efficiency in DNN workloads.
conditions: Workloads that stress memory-hierarchy traffic (typical DNN inference).
Reuse-friendly compute pattern such that on-chip storage enables data amortization.
nonImplications: Does not imply DRAM is always the energy bottleneck for every kernel; tiny in-cache workloads shift toward compute-energy.
Does not imply that adding SRAM automatically improves energy — reuse is required.

sourceMappings.locator: Ch. 1-2 relative energy per op in DNN accelerators

misconceptions.claim: FLOP minimization is the primary energy optimization for DNNs.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The dominant energy term is data movement, not FLOP count; a lower-FLOP model with worse locality can consume more energy.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: Sze et al., DNN efficient processing survey

misconceptions.claim: SRAM is always energy-cheaper than DRAM, so more SRAM always saves energy.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Per access, SRAM is cheaper; but if SRAM does not enable reuse (data still fetched fresh from DRAM), total energy does not fall.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: Sze et al., DNN accelerator energy analysis

misconceptions.claim: Quantization always halves energy for the same op count.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Energy savings from quantization require hardware support for the lower-precision datapath and matched Kernel; software emulation of low precision may increase energy.

implementationFacts: 45nm survey (Horowitz 2014): 32-bit DRAM access ≈ 640 pJ, 32-bit SRAM ≈ few pJ, 32-bit int MAC ≈ 3 pJ.
Weight-stationary / output-stationary dataflows are motivated by minimizing DRAM traffic per MAC.
performanceScenarios: Mobile inference chips (e.g., NPUs) heavily rely on on-chip weight caching to stay within a power budget.
